it plays Weather Control, you both take damage. In fact, you take the
damage right then and there. So is the taking of the damage considered
a "mini" damage resolution phase? And if it is, could you play Taste
of Vitae to reclaim the 1 point of lost blood at that moment prior to
the other phases of combat continuing? The current errata seems to
support this capability with - "Only counts blood that the opposing
vampire burned as a result of damage. It will not, for example, give

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <8kckr6$kpj$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>, Ramsteiner <ramsteiner@my-
deja.com> writes

>If it works as you state,
>then the use of Spawning Pool or Weather Control that sends opposing
>minions to torpor prior to the Strike phase and then the Damage
>Resolution phase would never be reached.

Each dealing of damage in a round has its own "mini" Damage Resolution
step, in order to allow Damage Prevention etc. cards to be played.
Clearly, in the case of Spawning Pool, the damage is not preventable,
but you still have to do Damage Resolution in order to see if the
vampire goes to torpor or not etc.

However, that isn't the same as strike resolution.

> Aside from S:CE, is this
>legal? Or would the damage be applied and cause the combat to rush
>through the other phases toward End of Combat?

What you are doing is assuming there can only be one "Damage Resolution"
in a combat. Clearly, there can be several. For instance, additional
strikes will cause a number of Damage Resolution phases - one for each
additional pair of strikes.

> If that is so, then you
>should still be able to play the ToV. Otherwise, you are correct, and
>no ToV could be played.

The combat goes like this:

First Round - Press to second round
Second Round:
- Tap Spawning Pool
- Resolve Damage
- Range
- Choose Strikes
- Resolve Strikes

Now, of course, a Strike: Combat Ends strike will abort the combat.
Since you never pass Strike Resolution, you cannot play Taste of Vitae.
However, if, say, your minion (probably a Nosferatu, but not required)
plays Immortal Grapple again, say, and both of you stay in combat, and
both hit each other then, after Strike Resolution you can:

- Play Taste of Vitae

Taste of Vitae will, of course, if you get there, count all the damage
from Spawning Pool since Taste of Vitae does not care for the source of
the damage - merely that the opponent suffered damage.

--
James Coupe (Prince of Mercia, England)

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In article <8kc3mb$97d$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>, legb...@my-deja.com writes

>i think the fact that it is not stated when during the second round you

I'll just go and check my actual card.... Okay, the card text file is
correct. (It's always difficult doing a ruling based on the card text
file and finding its wrong.)

The relevant card text is:

"If a
minion you control successfully blocks a bleed
against you and a second round of combat begins,
tap this card to inflict 1 damage to the acting minion
for each blood on the Spawning Pool. "

You have no option. It's not a "can" or a "may", it's an imperative -
"tap". Therefore:

If:
- the block is from a bleed
- you press to the second round
Then:
- tap the card there and then

Since you *have* to tap the card, you have to tap it at the earliest
opportunity - the very start of the second round. Else, you wouldn't be
able to guarantee tapping it.

The same logic applies to commiting yourself to strike with a gun by
maneuvering with it. Since you could not guarantee being around for an
additional strike (as you could not guarantee being around later in the
round to tap the card[0]), you have to do it now.

[0] For instance, three of us are playing on the table, Carol, Bob and I
(that order). Bob has a Madness Network in play and so bleeds me at the
end of Carol's turn with Zebulon. I block, first round goes and we go
to the second round. If you delayed playing it, the following could
happen: We choose strikes. Zebulon says hands and I say hands. Then,
Zebulon, as acting minion, has priority to play the next effect. He
chooses Wolf Claws. Then, he still has priority, so his Methuselah,
Bob, plays Rotschreck. Due to card text, Combat Ends. At that point, I
am ineligible to tap Spawning Pool, and so have failed to do what is
required by the card - tap it.

expressed by the text "a second round of combat begins") but that tapping is
not required. If you don't tap then, though, you lose the opportunity to do
so until a future combat ensues (and goes to the beginning of a second
round, as well...)

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
hel...@my-deja.com wrote:
> 1. If a vamp blocks a bleed, completes combat in the first round, and
> a second vamp fast reacts, and presses combat to a second round, can
> the Spawning Pool be utilised?

No. It can only be utilized in the block-induced combat.

> 2. If in a combat the Spawning Pool is utilised, resulting in the
> opposing vampire heading to torpor, can Taste of Vitae be played to
> gain the blood lost by the opposing vampire? Taste reads that it must
> be played after strike resolution. If the opposing vampire goes
> torporous at the start of the round, does the combat ever get to strike
> resolution?

No. If combat ends before strikes resolve, then combat never gets
to strike resolution.

But, if you tap Spawning Pool to deal damage during strike resolution
(or immedaitely after), you can Taste the blood lost to the damage.

Messages.Author: Noal McDonald
Messages.Body:
>> Ok. Now I have a problem with the above statement. If the action
>> is still pending (as you stated above citing Freak Drive) how does
>> Form of Mist at superior get screwed from being played to continue
>> the action?
>
> As stated above, referring to the rule against adding stealth
> when stealth is not needed.

How is that you are able to make that assertion? Clearly, the minion
needs the stealth to continue the action. How is this any different from
a target tapping his last untapped minion to block and using Form of
Mist when he no longer has any untapped minions to block
with...resulting in a lack of need for the stealth?

Let's use that as example 1:

Vamp A bleeds
Vamp B blocks (the prey's only vampire, for the sake of discussion)

Vamp A uses FoM to continue the action

Let's use Sorrow's illustration as exmaple 2:

Vamp A bleeds
Vamp B blocks
Vamp A Strikes: Earth Meld
Vamp C uses Fast Reaction
Vamp A uses FoM to continue the action

First off, are you saying that using the Form of Mist results in an
unsuccessful block and does not leave the blocker tapped? If that was
the case, the Vamp B in both examples would still be untapped and Vamp A
would need the stealth to make the action resolve successfully.

However, according to the on-line rulebook, that's not the case at all.
I refer you to:

6.2.3. Resolve the Action
If the action is blocked, then any card played to take the action is
burned and the blocking minion is tapped and enters combat with the
acting minion (see Combat, sec. 6.4).
6.4. Combat
Combat results when a minion blocks the action of a ready minion.

These exerpts make it clear that a Vamp B has to succesfully block Vamp
A _and_ tap before combat even begins. Which means that Vamp B is not a
valid blocker (barring a wake) and cannot even attempt to block the Vamp
A again. Wether Vamp C enters combat with Vamp A with Fast Reaction is
irrelevent per the following:

6.2.3. Resolve the Action
Once the combat is resolved, the action is over.

Which means the action was resolved at the end of the initial combat in
both circumstances and strongly infers that the second attempt using
Form of Mist is actually a seperate action entirely. Note that this
technically violates NRA and pretty much means that a minion that used
FA or WWEF to block can't attempt to block a 2nd time (without an
additional wake) because the action had already resolved.

So...either the rulebook is wrong and that the initial action did not
resolve with the end of the first combat and that by its very nature,
Form of Mist violates the ban on pushing stealth..._or_...the use of
Psyche and Fast Reactions is completely irrelevant as the stealth is
still required to attempt to successfully resolve the action.

Regards,
Noal

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Noal McDonald <dhar...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> > As stated above, referring to the rule against adding stealth
> > when stealth is not needed.
>
> How is that you are able to make that assertion? Clearly, the minion

> needs the stealth to continue the action. How is this different from

> a target tapping his last untapped minion to block and using Form of
> Mist when he no longer has any untapped minions to block
> with...resulting in a lack of need for the stealth?

It is different in that there is a current blocking minion.
When in combat with a non-blocking minion, there is no current
blocking minion.

The criterion for "needs stealth" is currently:
"there is a current blocking minion with intercept equal to
or exceeding the acting minion's stealth."

With no current blocking minion (as in the case of Fast Reaction
combat), the acting minion doesn't "need stealth".

> Let's use that as example 1:

> Vamp B blocks (the prey's only vampire, for the sake of discussion)
> Vamp A uses FoM to continue the action

anything of the sort. Please explain the basis for the question.

A

all.

> 6.4. Combat

Vamp
> A _and_ tap before combat even begins.

Right. I never suggested otherwise.

> Which means that Vamp B is not a
> valid blocker (barring a wake) and cannot even attempt to block the
Vamp
> A again.

Right. Again, I never suggested otherwise.
But Vamp B is the blocking minion in combat, even while tapped.

> Wether Vamp C enters combat with Vamp A with Fast Reaction is
> irrelevent per the following:
>
> 6.2.3. Resolve the Action
> Once the combat is resolved, the action is over.
>
> Which means the action was resolved at the end of the initial combat
in
> both circumstances and strongly infers that the second attempt using
> Form of Mist is actually a seperate action entirely. Note that this
> technically violates NRA and pretty much means that a minion that used
> FA or WWEF to block can't attempt to block a 2nd time (without an
> additional wake) because the action had already resolved.

Yes, the rulebook doesn't cover the multiple-combat cases adequately.
The action isn't actually over until all of the effects to be handled
during the action are concluded. Putting such text in the rulebook
would only confuse the player attempting to learn how to play the
game.

A strict reading of the rulebook text would preclude the use
of Cats Guidance or Freak Drive to untap after combat.

> So...either the rulebook is wrong and that the initial action did not
> resolve with the end of the first combat and that by its very nature,
> Form of Mist violates the ban on pushing stealth..._or_...the use of
> Psyche and Fast Reactions is completely irrelevant as the stealth is
> still required to attempt to successfully resolve the action.

The rulebook is "wrong" for these cases, but FoM doesn't get to
violate the ban on "pushing" stealth. The only option (other than
the current ruling) is to agree with you that, once tapped, the
blocking minion ceases to qualify the acting minion as "needing
stealth", and therefore superior Form of Mist could never be
played to continue an action.
